source.title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Antibody Language Models Using SAEs
source.authors: Rebonto Haque; Oliver M. Turnbull; Anisha Parsan; Nithin Parsan; John J. Yang; Anna L. Beukenhorst; Charlotte M. Deane

record.tranche_reason: The study uses neuron activations as a baseline and invokes neuron polysemanticity as a rationale for SAE analysis, but it does not measure the share of neuron poles with one or more jobs or test the other claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper compares neuron activations with SAE latents for antibody-sequence concepts. Those neuron-specific findings are recorded under fits_no_version because the claim versions do not specify this comparison or its measures. Results about SAE steering, including results on other antibody models, do not test the listed neuron-pole or explanation-scoring versions. Cited findings from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study trains SAEs on antibody language models and reports SAE latent interpretability and steering. Its only neuron results are a probe accuracy (0.98 vs 0.99 for latents) and a qualitative plot of the top CDRH3-correlated neurons. Neither counts neuron poles by job, scores neuron explanations, or tests the other versions. It invokes neuron polysemanticity as motivation (Sec. 2.2, 4.1.2) without measuring it.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that TopK SAEs find interpretable antibody-specific latents (CDR and germline-gene identity), but high correlation with a concept does not ensure steerability. Ordered SAEs reliably give steerable features, at the cost of less interpretable activation patterns. They also report these qualitative findings replicate on IgLM and ProGen2-OAS.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains and probes TopK and Ordered SAEs on antibody language models and compares neuron activations with SAE latents; it does not reproduce a neuron-pole audit or explanation-scoring procedure.

fits_no_version.finding: In p-IgGen layer 3, a linear probe on hidden-neuron activations reached 0.98 validation accuracy for residue-level CDR identity, versus 0.99 for TopK SAE latents.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Neuron activations in a small antibody language model jointly encode CDR identity about as well as SAE latents.

fits_no_version.finding: The top CDRH3-correlated neurons in p-IgGen fired scattered across the sequence, while TopK SAE latents localized to CDRH3 residues (Figure 1a).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In a 17M antibody language model, the top concept-correlated neurons look less localized than SAE latents for CDRH3, a single qualitative example.

record.problems: The neuron-specific evidence is limited to one antibody model and a qualitative activation-pattern comparison plus a CDR-identity prediction accuracy. Neither result counts neuron poles or tests their individual jobs. The stated code and data access is through a private Zenodo link.
record.rows_left_out: No additional neuron-specific results bearing on the listed versions were reported. SAE feature and steering results were left out because they do not measure the claim's neuron-pole or explanation-scoring outcomes.

untested.parts: No neuron-pole audit of Qwen3-32B or any model.
No shares of interpretable neurons across models or scales; the other antibody models are analysed only with SAEs.
No vision neurons, InceptionV1, pose or recursive generalization.
No test of architecture, regularization or tools as causes of neuron interpretability.
No neuron-based attribution graphs or reconstruction-error comparison.
No test of whether explanations fitting activating examples predict firing.
No simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T4 / uses_without_test classification is confirmed. The neuron-versus-latent comparison is a single qualitative example in a 17M non-text model, with no count of interpretable neurons, so it bears on no version. Neither original source is involved.

versions.untested_parts: Does not audit neuron poles, count poles by number of jobs, or estimate the share of poles understood in Qwen3-32B or another model.
Does not measure shares of interpretable neuron poles across model families or scales, including dense and mixture-of-experts models or trillion-parameter models.
Does not analyze InceptionV1 cat-and-car neurons, pose, or recursive generalization.
Does not test whether architecture, regularization, or tools explain changes in neuron interpretability, or estimate interpretable-neuron shares for vision models.
Does not construct attribution graphs from a large model's own neurons or evaluate their reconstruction error.
Does not test explanations against held-out activating examples or measure whether explanations predict where neurons fire.
Does not score neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

rows.subject: p-IgGen
rows.stage_stated: autoregressive antibody language model trained on paired OAS
rows.operation_detail: A logistic regressor used hidden-neuron activations to predict CDR identity.
rows.note: The paper reports that neuron activations retain CDR-identity information; this prediction accuracy does not measure how many neuron poles have a main job.
rows.check: Linear-probe accuracy on all neurons jointly measures information content, not per-neuron jobs. Comparator to the study's SAE method; not a test of any version.

rows.subject: p-IgGen
rows.stage_stated: autoregressive antibody language model trained on paired OAS
rows.operation_detail: Compared visual activation patterns of neurons and SAE latents for CDRH3 identity.
rows.measure: Qualitative localization and recognizability of activation patterns along antibody sequences
rows.baseline: TopK latent activations localize to CDRH3 residues
rows.value: Neuron activations occur across the sequence without an immediately recognizable pattern
rows.note: The authors suggest polysemanticity may explain the scattered neuron patterns. This is a qualitative observation, not a pole-by-pole job audit.
rows.check: Qualitative look at top-correlated neurons for one concept in a 17M antibody model. No share of interpretable neurons and no explanation scoring. Polysemanticity is the authors' speculation, not a measured result.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
